    Rate of introduction from first records, allowing for discovery effort

    Source: R/inv-niche.R
    inv_discovery_rate.Rd

    The number of alien species first recorded each year rises with both the rate of introduction and the effort put into finding them. Solow and Costello (2004) separate the two: species arrive at rate \(\mu_t = \exp(\beta_0 + \beta_1 t)\), and each undiscovered species is found in year t with probability \(\pi_t = \mathrm{logit}^{-1}(\gamma_0 + \gamma_1 t)\), so the expected first records in year t are \(\lambda_t = \sum_{s \le t} \mu_s \pi_t \prod_{r=s}^{t-1}(1 - \pi_r)\). The four parameters are fitted by Poisson maximum likelihood. A positive beta_1 means introductions are accelerating even after allowing for growing discovery effort; a positive gamma_1 means detection has improved.

    Time runs from the first year in the data, so years before the first record are included only when given as rows with a count of zero. The two rates are only weakly separable with short records; check the widths of the intervals.

    Usage

    inv_discovery_rate(.data, year, count = NULL, conf_level = 0.95)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per species (with the year of its first record) or one row per year (with a count).

    year

    <tidy-select> Column with the year.

    count

    <tidy-select> Optional column with the number of first records in each year. Without it each row is one species.

    conf_level

    Confidence level of the Wald intervals.

    Value

    A tibble of class inv_discovery with one row per year: year, observed, expected (fitted first records), introduced (estimated introductions) and detection (discovery probability). The attribute "coefficients" holds a tibble of the four parameters with standard errors and intervals, and "undiscovered" the expected number of species introduced but not yet recorded by the last year.

    References

    Solow, A. R. and Costello, C. J. (2004). Estimating the rate of species introductions from the discovery record. Ecology, 85, 1822-1825. doi:10.1890/03-3102

    Examples

    set.seed(4)
yrs <- 1900:2000
mu <- exp(-1 + 0.025 * (yrs - 1900))
pi_t <- plogis(-3 + 0.03 * (yrs - 1900))
# Undiscovered species accumulate and are found with probability pi_t
pool <- 0
lam <- numeric(length(yrs))
for (t in seq_along(yrs)) {
  pool <- pool + mu[t]
  lam[t] <- pool * pi_t[t]
  pool <- pool * (1 - pi_t[t])
}
records <- data.frame(year = yrs, n = rpois(length(yrs), lam))
fit <- inv_discovery_rate(records, year, count = n)
attr(fit, "coefficients")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   term    estimate std_error conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 beta_0   -0.245     2.30    -4.75      4.26  
#> 2 beta_1    0.0158    0.0206  -0.0246    0.0562
#> 3 gamma_0  -2.98      2.12    -7.13      1.16  
#> 4 gamma_1   0.0147    0.0953  -0.172     0.201
